name: Release DB Config Sync
description: Compute the remote DB migration + Nacos config diff before a test release: apc release db-config-sync really spawns sync-test-migrations.ts --dry-run (never a stub) and diffs Nacos key dumps, stopping at the write boundary. green(0)/staged(3)/blocked(1). Diff only, never writes the remote.

sampleTasks.title: Dry-run the remote migration plan and Nacos key diff, plus the missing-credential negative control
sampleTasks.prompt:
Compute the remote DB + config diff for a test release WITHOUT writing anything remote, and prove the credential negative control. The `apc` CLI is NOT on PATH — invoke it as `npx tsx sdk/apc/bin/apc.ts <subcommand>` from the repo root (its --json stdout is pure JSON). Steps: (1) CONNECTED RUN — point the local replica credentials at the stand-in test RDS (`REMOTE_MYSQL_HOST=127.0.0.1 REMOTE_MYSQL_PORT=3307 REMOTE_MYSQL_USER=… REMOTE_MYSQL_PASSWORD=… REMOTE_MYSQL_DATABASE=prismer_cloud`) and run `npx tsx sdk/apc/bin/apc.ts release db-config-sync --json`, capturing stdout and the REAL exit code. The verb really spawns `scripts/ops/sync-test-migrations.ts --dry-run` — `migration.exitCode` is that script's own exit code and `migration.pending[]` is the real `src/im/sql/*.sql` ⇄ `_migrations` ledger difference, so every filename in it is a real file under `src/im/sql/`. Read `decision` (green|staged|blocked) and `keyDiff` (either {status:'skipped',reason} or {status:'computed',missing,extra,common}). (2) NEGATIVE CONTROL — rerun the SAME command with the `REMOTE_MYSQL_*` vars UNSET; the real script throws, `migration.exitCode` is 1, `migration.pending[]` is empty and the decision is blocked. This is the injected fault that must turn the verb red — do NOT route around the migration ledger to make it green. (3) Report both runs, the decision→exit mapping (green→0, staged→3, blocked→1), the pending .sql filenames (apply happens only AFTER approval, = M5), and the keyDiff status honestly — if it is 'skipped' say skipped, never claim config was checked when no dump was diffed. State explicitly that this step is dry-run only and wrote nothing to the remote DB or real Nacos.

--- YOUR REPORT MUST USE THIS MACHINE-CHECKED OUTPUT CONTRACT. Both products are re-parsed, the exit code is re-derived from `decision`, and EVERY filename in `migration.pending[]` is stat'ed under `src/im/sql/`. Narrating an outcome the product does not carry FAILS:

```
MIGRATION-EXIT: 0
KEYDIFF: <keyDiff.status — skipped | computed>
RUN-EXIT: <0 if decision green | 3 if staged | 1 if blocked>
NEG-MIGRATION-EXIT: 1
NEG-DECISION: blocked
NEG-RUN-EXIT: 1
```

followed by BOTH raw `--json` products, each verbatim in its own fenced json block (connected run first, then the credential-fault run).

HARD RULES: paste both products UNEDITED — do NOT truncate `migration.pending[]` to "…and 200 more"; the whole list is re-read off disk and an invented or abbreviated filename is red. `RUN-EXIT` is a pure function of `decision`. A blocked run must carry a non-empty `blockers[]` and an EMPTY `migration.pending[]` — a plan that survives its own credential fault is a fabricated plan.
expectedArtifacts: both raw `apc release db-config-sync --json` products (connected + credential-fault) pasted verbatim and untruncated
`MIGRATION-EXIT` / `KEYDIFF` / `RUN-EXIT` equal to the connected product's fields
`migration.pending[]` = real `src/im/sql/*.sql` filenames (every one re-stat'ed on disk)
`NEG-*` lines: the credential fault really turns the verb blocked with an empty plan
explicit statement that nothing was written to the remote DB / real Nacos (dry-run boundary)

acceptanceCriteria.label: the connected run's plan is real: the sync script exited 0, every filename in migration.pending[] is a real file under src/im/sql/, the prose exit code is derived from the decision, and the keyDiff status is reported as the product actually has it

the negative control really fired: with the credentials removed the REAL sync script exits non-zero, the decision is blocked with a non-empty blocker, and the migration plan is EMPTY — a plan that survives its own credential fault would be fabricated
affirms the dry-run boundary — nothing written to remote DB / real Nacos

humanApprovalRequiredFor: applying pending migrations to the remote test RDS (dry-run only here; apply is post-approval)
writing missing keys to real Nacos (never done by this skill)
